post_slowdown_asr_text: A note saying delivery was missed was left at the home of someone who had chosen a morning time too. For people who can choose how to get packages, a re-delivery fee can be a sign that encourages them to make an effort. But making the person who gets the package pay will not fix late deliveries or the way people are told when packages will arrive. People who get packages cannot change the delivery cost. They also cannot decide how much of it goes to delivery workers. When you could not be home and had a problem, could you choose how to get your package? Did you know when it would arrive? Can charging the person who gets the package fix that problem?
